author: Al Jazeera English
description:
The planned opening of the Gordie Howe International Bridge between Detroit and Windsor has become another flashpoint in the growing trade dispute between the United States and Canada.
The $4.5bn crossing, built to strengthen one of the world’s biggest trading relationships, has been delayed by US President Donald Trump.
The bridge was designed to ease pressure on the century-old Ambassador Bridge, which handles a major share of North American land trade.
Canadian officials and business leaders warn that tariffs and trade tensions are damaging deeply integrated supply chains, especially in the auto industry.
The dispute comes as Trump questions the benefits of decades of economic integration with Canada.
Despite the tensions, billions of dollars in goods continue to cross the border every day between the two allies.

Al Jazeera’s Ian Wood reports from Windsor, Canada.

US President Donald Trump will meet Lebanon’s President Joseph Aoun in Washington, DC later on Tuesday.
It’s the first time in nearly two decades that a Lebanese president is visiting the White House. 
It follows a US-brokered agreement between Lebanon and Israel that calls for disarming Hezbollah and the gradual withdrawal of Israeli troops.
Lebanese authorities believe diplomacy with Israel is the only viable path to regaining sovereignty and ending the conflict.
But it’s a decision that divided the country.
